sources.entry: django-unfold - A modern Django admin theme for building dashboards, internal tools, and business applications.

summary.one_liner: Unfold is a modern, Tailwind CSS-based theme for the Django admin, aimed at dashboards, internal tools, and business back-office applications.
summary.what_it_does: Unfold replaces the look of Django's built-in admin while staying on django.contrib.admin, so existing models, permissions, and conventions carry over. You install it, add "unfold" to INSTALLED_APPS, and subclass its ModelAdmin in your admin classes. The README describes dark mode, customizable colors and layout options, and a sidebar with navigation and tabs for models, fieldsets, and inlines. It also lists advanced changelist filters (dropdown, autocomplete, date range, facet, and others), global, row-level, detail and dropdown actions, and form features such as conditional fields, sortable inlines, WYSIWYG editing, and django-crispy-forms support. The README names built-in integrations for a set of third-party Django packages, including django-import-export, django-guardian, django-simple-history, and django-constance, each with an integration guide.
use_cases: add dashboards with charts and cards to Django admin
integrate django-import-export or django-simple-history into admin
incrementally restyle an existing Django admin
how_to_run: Add "unfold" as the first entry in INSTALLED_APPS
Subclass ModelAdmin in your admin class, e.g. @admin.register(MyModel) class MyModelAdmin(ModelAdmin): pass
notable: Built on django.contrib.admin, so it is a drop-in theme rather than a replacement admin framework
Supports incremental adoption without rebuilding the existing admin
Custom dashboard pages with reusable cards, charts and buttons
Documented integrations for about a dozen third-party Django packages
caveats: The README does not state any platform limits or paid tiers
Setup requires Django and the "unfold" app to be configured in INSTALLED_APPS, with ModelAdmin subclassed per model
Third-party integrations are listed with separate guides; support depends on those packages being installed
